free_tier.stated: 10 GiB free storage per project on GitLab.com Free tier (repo + LFS); snippet files up to 50 MB each (50,000,000-byte default admin limit); projects per account and accounts are free.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: unmetered, served from gitlab.com; no egress line item exists on any GitLab.com plan.

tooling: glab CLI (glab snippet create), VS Code extension, REST /api/v4/snippets, plain git clone/push for project repos. rclone has a 'gitlab' backend (yes — rclone supports GitLab as a Git remote type via backend 'git').
chaining: 10 GiB free per project x unlimited projects per free account x unlimited free accounts. Snippets add a parallel 50 MB-per-object path that does not require a project. 10 TiB hot = ~1000 projects at 10 GiB, spread over accounts.
limits_note: 10 GiB per project then the project goes read-only (pushes rejected) until storage is purchased — a hard stop, not a warning; 50 MB per snippet; namespace storage updated every 90 minutes; 5 GiB per-file push limit on gitlab.com is not documented publicly, so shard files.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Read-only lockout is automatic and immediate on exceeding 10 GiB, and it blocks pushes rather than deletes data. Snippets are counted in namespace storage, so they are not a separate free pool.
